subject: Production traffic policing triggered for Avenue Health — urgent
messages:
From: Mark Spencer <mark@avenuehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: High 429s + latency in production after morning deploy

Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and tail latency on our integration after your early morning deploy (around 06:00 PDT). Impact is across our checkout and order-normalization endpoints; throughput drops and retries are spiking. Our engineers are blocked and customers are complaining.

Screenshot attached showing spike and sample timestamps. Can you confirm if anything changed to rate limiting, quotas, or burst settings for our account? We are on a Dedicated plan and expect predictable throughput.

Urgent please — we are evaluating fallbacks on our side but need an immediate remediation plan.

Thanks,
Mark Spencer
Head of Ops, Avenue Health
[Attachment: customer-screenshot-429.png (png, 430KB)]

Hi Mark — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption.

I am escalating to SRE and CS immediately. Can you paste one example request ID and a couple of timestamps from the logs? Also confirming: you are on the dedicated capacity pool AH-dedicated-2, correct?

I will coordinate an emergency plan: temporary quota bump or short rollback if needed. Monica and Laura, please triage and loop in infra.

Would you be available for a 15-minute call at 08:40 PT?

Karthik

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 09:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: High 429s + latency in production after morning deploy

Quick initial triage notes (internal):
- I reviewed the traffic dump and our policy diff from this morning. There was a config push that intended to tighten policing for free-tier customers but the selector match was overly broad.
- The per-customer window key was evaluated as the more restrictive per-instance key due to an ordering bug in the policy engine; AH traffic ended up matched to a global policing rule that enforces 1 req/s with a 2-request burst.
- This explains the sudden surge of 429s and long queuing on the runtime.

Temporary mitigation options:
1) Apply an emergency policy override that scopes the policing rule to 'tier: free' only (safe, immediate).
2) Increase AH's allowance to 10 req/s with a 50-request burst for the next 2 hours.
3) Roll back the morning policy push entirely (coarser but full rollback).

I favor option 1 for minimal blast radius. Rafael — can infra apply the policy override? Vanessa — can we prepare a quick canary to validate?

LA
Product Ops

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Mark Spencer <mark@avenuehealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 09:18:07 -0700
Subject: Re: High 429s + latency in production after morning deploy

Mark — we are on it. Our immediate customer-facing plan: 1) apply temporary allowance for Avenue Health to reduce 429s, 2) monitor for 30 minutes and restore normal policing once stabilized, 3) schedule RCA and share a timeline for credits.

Can you confirm the business critical windows today (times when you must have full throughput) so we avoid making changes during peak? Also, please send any request IDs you have from the 08:00–08:15 window.

We will aim to have the temporary allowance live within 20 minutes.

— Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2027 09:29:55 -0700
Subject: Re: High 429s + latency in production after morning deploy

On my side: I will push an emergency policy override to the config cluster. Steps:
- Add policy override: scope=customer:avenue-health -> rate_limit=10r/s, burst=50
- Pin override to AH-dedicated-2 routing rule to avoid global exposure
- Deploy config patch id 'cfg-em-20270619-01' to staging and then to prod (rolling) — expected propagation 45–90s to policy caches
- If caches show errors, we will fallback to rollback of morning push.

Command snippet (infra runbook):
sudo redwoodctl config apply --file policies/overrides/avenue-health-allow.yaml --patch-id cfg-em-20270619-01

I will run the change in 2 minutes. There will be a short policy cache refresh but no service restart required. If we need a hard restart it's <60s and we'll communicate.

[Attachment: policies.yaml (yaml, 6KB) — emergency override draft]

RM

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Mark Spencer <mark@avenuehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Resolved: temporary allowance applied and monitoring; RCA next steps

Mark — we applied an emergency override last night at 09:31 PT that moved Avenue Health to a temporary allowance (10 req/s with 50 burst) and pinned the rule to your dedicated pool. You should see 429s drop immediately; our telemetry shows error rate back to baseline and tail latency improved.

Next steps:
- We scheduled a technical RCA with Product, SRE, and CS for Monday 09:00 PT to review the policy engine bug and test a safe rollout for the original morning change.
- We will propose a one-time service credit for the incident; Monica will follow up with the proposed credit amount and timeline.
- We will push a fix to the policy engine to avoid selector ordering regressions and add a pre-deploy validation for customer-scoped rules.

Appreciate your patience — sorry again for the impact. Please reply if you still see anomalies; Monica will be your primary contact for follow-up.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
